There was no natural light in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station.

The text of the judgment of 13 December 2008 did not specify which particular words Mr Nagibin had pronounced.

The Justice of the Peace did not address Mr Nagibin's arguments that he had not used foul language but rather had been making a solo demonstration when the police officers came and ordered him to stop the unlawful demonstration.
The Justice of the Peace sentenced Mr Nagibin to three days' administrative imprisonment, to be calculated from 7.35 p.m. on 12 December 2008.

On 12 January 2009 the Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu upheld Mr Nagibin's conviction of 13 December 2008.
On 25 March 2009 the Pervomayskiy District Court rejected Mr Nagibin's claim for inclusion of the time period from 5.48 p.m. to 7.35 p.m. on 12 December 2008 in the period of his detention.
The Pervomayskiy District Court held on 25 March 2009 that it was not reliably shown that Mr Nagibin had been detained at 5.48 p.m. on 12 December 2008.
On 28 May 2009 the Rostov Regional Court upheld the Pervomayskiy District Court's decision of 25 March 2009 on appeal.
Mr Nagibin complained to a court about poor conditions of his detention in the night from 12 to 13 December 2008 on the premises of the Kirovskiy district police station.
Mr Nagibin argued that he had no sleeping place during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station in the night from 12 to 13 December 2008.
Mr Nagibin argued that on 13 December 2008 he was transported in an unheated minivan for more than two hours.
Mr Nagibin argued that he had not received any food on 13 December 2008.
On 25 March 2009 the Pervomayskiy District Court rejected Mr Nagibin's complaints about the conditions of his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station.
The Pervomayskiy District Court found on 25 March 2009 that Mr Nagibin had been provided with a sleeping place on a bench and bed linen during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station.
The Pervomayskiy District Court found on 25 March 2009 that Mr Nagibin had been given packed food provisions on 12 and 13 December 2008.
The Pervomayskiy District Court accepted the police representative's submission that the car used to transport Mr Nagibin on 13 December 2008 had been 'specifically equipped' for transporting people.
On 28 May 2009 the Rostov Regional Court upheld the Pervomayskiy District Court's judgment of 25 March 2009 on appeal.
